papers.title: Ultrasparse Ultrasparsifiers and Faster Laplacian System Solvers
papers.abstract: In this article, we provide an O(m loglogO(1) n log (1/ε))-expected time algorithm for solving Laplacian systems on n-node m-edge graphs, improving upon the previous best expected runtime of O(m sqrt{log n} loglog^{O(1)} n log (1/ε)) achieved by Cohen et al. To obtain this result, we provide efficient constructions of low spectral stretch graph approximations with improved stretch and sparsity bounds. As motivation for this work, we show that, for every set of vectors in R^d (not just those induced by graphs) and all integer k > 1, there exist an ultra-sparsifier with d-1 + O(d/k) re-weighted vectors of relative condition number at most k^2. For small k, this improves upon the previous best known multiplicative factor of k * O~(log d), which is only known for the graph case. Additionally, in the graph case, we employ our low-stretch subgraph construction to obtain n - 1 + O(n/k)-edge ultrasparsifiers of relative condition number k^{1+o(1)} for k = ω(log^δ n) for any δ > 0: this improves upon the previous work for k = o(exp(log^{1/2-δ} n)).

papers.title: Peeling Close to the Orientability Threshold Spatial Coupling in Hashing-Based Data Structures
papers.abstract: In multiple-choice data structures each element x is associated with a set e(x) ⊆ [n] of size ℓ ≥ 1, and one considers the hypergraph H = ([n],{e(x) | x∈ S}). In many applications, it is desirable that H admits a peeling sequence, i.e. an ordering of the edges such that every edge has a vertex of degree 1 at the time it is removed. Many hypergraphs exhibit sharp density thresholds with respect to the property of ℓ-orientability and peeling. We propose a new kind of distribution for hyperedges that results in hypergraphs which are orientable and peelable all the way up to the orientability threshold. Our construction is simple: The hypergraph H consists of nk (slightly overlapping) copies of a hypergraph H0 of constant size. We demonstrate the usefulness of our construction using our hypergraphs as a drop-in replacement in a retrieval data structure by Botelho et al. This reduces memory usage from ≈1.23m to ≈1.12m for m entries and any k > 3.
